name: Poultry farms (broiler and layer)

problems.words: Mortality is shown on the board but I think workers under-report
quick_ideas: Count mortality at one fixed time each day with a photo
At flock end, check birds placed minus deaths against birds lifted.

workzap_build.text: nori_daily_read — daily mortality entered per shed with photo, rolled into the owner's morning read and checked against placement on the spot.

problems.ask_first: Who counts and records deaths each day?
problems.free_stops: How counts are checked against placement and lifting goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the board total with one walk through the shed and your own rough count, so under-reporting shows before flock end.
Give one person the job of writing mortality in one notebook at one fixed time, so the board matches one source all week.

problems.words: Rate gir gaya jab lifting ka time aaya, sara profit chala gaya
quick_ideas: Note the published daily rate next to your own sale rate
Speak to more than one buyer before lifting day.

workzap_build.text: a daily rate log compared directly with the farm's sale rates flock after flock.

problems.ask_first: How is the rate decided on lifting day?
problems.free_stops: How rates are collected and compared stays in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the rate discussed before lifting and the rate used at lifting side by side, so the drop is clear in your own record.
Give one person the job of noting every buyer rate in one notebook before lifting week, so sale talks stop relying on memory.

problems.words: Dealer gives feed on credit then forces his rate when he buys the birds
quick_ideas: Keep your own record of everything taken on credit and the rate given at lifting
Ask for a written settlement at the end of each flock.

workzap_build.text: a dealer ledger of chicks, feed and other items on credit, birds lifted, weights, rates and balance, settled flock by flock without delay.

problems.ask_first: Does the dealer also owe you from earlier flocks?
problems.free_stops: The ledger layout and settlement check are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the dealer's credit entries with your own notebook of each delivery and settlement, so forced rate cuts are easier to challenge.
Give one person the job of keeping all credit notes and lifting settlements in one place, so each flock closes with fewer surprises.

problems.words: Feed bags received don't match the bill
quick_ideas: Count bags off the truck before signing
Match the count to the bill the same day.

workzap_build.text: bags received vs billed logged with photo of the slip, and mismatches flagged to the owner right away.

problems.ask_first: Who receives feed at each farm?
problems.free_stops: The receiving log and flag rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count the bags on the truck beside the bill before unloading finishes, so any short delivery is caught while the driver is there.
Give one worker the job of noting each delivery count in one notebook at unloading, so the bill can be checked the same day.

problems.words: Feed runs out on a Sunday and we wait two days
quick_ideas: Count bags left each evening so a run-out shows early
Keep a weekend contact for your feed supplier.

workzap_build.text: feed stock per shed kept running daily with days-left and a reorder alert sent when low.

problems.ask_first: How many days' feed do you usually keep?
problems.free_stops: How days-left and reorder points are worked out stays in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note evening bags left beside the usual daily use for each shed, so a Sunday runout is visible earlier in the week.
Give one person the job of writing remaining bags in one notebook every evening, so reorder timing stops shifting between workers.

problems.words: I don't know my FCR until the flock is sold
quick_ideas: Note feed issued per shed every day
Weigh sample birds as your company technical team or vet suggests, so the numbers exist mid-flock.

workzap_build.text: a running FCR and cost-per-bird view updated daily from the farm's own entries.

problems.ask_first: Are feed issues written per shed or for the whole farm?
problems.free_stops: How the running figures are calculated is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare feed issued this week with the last flock at the same stage, so unusual usage is seen before sale day.
Give one person the job of writing feed issued per shed in one notebook each day, so mid-flock review is possible with your team.

problems.words: Generator failed at night in summer and we lost birds
quick_ideas: Check the generator starts every day
Make sure the night worker knows exactly who to call.

workzap_build.text: workflow_routine — a night-round checklist with timestamps and a generator log, alerting the owner right away when a round is missed.

problems.ask_first: How do you find out about a failure at night today?
problems.free_stops: Round timings and alert routing go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every night start issue and delay in one notebook this week, so the weak point around generator failure is easier to spot.
Give the night worker one written call list kept beside the generator, so breakdowns move faster when the power fails.

problems.words: Eggs break or go missing between shed and loading
quick_ideas: Count trays at the shed and again at loading
Note breakages where they happen.

workzap_build.text: field_checks — egg counts logged at shed, store and truck, with gaps flagged to the owner each day.

problems.ask_first: Where do the shortages usually show up?
problems.free_stops: The count points and gap rules stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare trays counted at the shed with trays counted at loading each day, so the loss point between handovers gets clearer.
Give one person the job of recording breakage and missing trays in one notebook at each handover, so blame stops shifting later.

problems.words: Integrator's settlement sheet is a mystery to me
quick_ideas: Keep your own copy of chicks placed, feed received, deaths and birds lifted
Ask for each deduction to be explained in writing; for the contract itself, talk to your accountant or lawyer.

workzap_build.text: a flock record built from the farm's own entries, set beside the settlement sheet so differences stand out.

problems.ask_first: Which part of the settlement is hardest to follow?
problems.free_stops: How the comparison is laid out goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each line on the settlement sheet beside your own flock figures, so the deductions that drive your margin stand out.
Give one person the job of keeping chicks placed, feed received, deaths and birds lifted in one notebook, so settlement checking becomes quicker.

problems.words: I run three farms and get updates by voice note only
quick_ideas: Ask each farm for the day's numbers in one written message
Use the same few numbers for every farm so they can be compared.

workzap_build.text: one morning read sent across all farms with mortality, feed left, power issues and cash.

problems.ask_first: Who sends updates from each farm?
problems.free_stops: Which numbers go in and how farms are compared is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each farm's voice note against one notebook page of daily key numbers, so weak updates stand out before a problem grows.
Give one supervisor the job of sending each farm's daily numbers at one fixed time, so you stop chasing updates across three farms.

never_say: Any vaccine, medicine, antibiotic, dosing, withdrawal time, feed formula, lighting programme or biosecurity advice; suggest their vet or company technical team.
Any disease diagnosis (Newcastle, bird flu, gumboro); for a suspected outbreak, suggest their vet and livestock department now.
Anything that helps sell birds or eggs that should be withheld, hide mortality from integrators or insurers, or dodge environment or food rules.
Predictions of rates or flock profit.
Advice on quota or marketing board rules in Canada, or covert surveillance of workers.

sample_reply.person: 3 broiler sheds hain Sheikhupura mein, daana dealer se udhaar pe aata hai aur wohi apna rate laga ke birds uthata hai. Har flock mein loss. Kya karein?
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur is ke liye bade kharch ki zaroorat nahi.
Pehle, udhaar pe aane wali har cheez aur lifting ke din ka rate aur wazan apne paas alag likhein.
Doosra, har roz akhbar ya WhatsApp wala rate bhi saath likhein, taake lifting rate se mila kar dekha ja sake.
Workzap is se aage ye kar sakta hai: dealer ka ledger aur flock register jo udhaar, lifting, rate aur har flock ka asal nateeja roz aik jagah dikhaye.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
